name: Should the addition design include future resale in mind?

mainEntity.name: How much should I design for my own needs versus what future buyers might want?
mainEntity.text: How much should I design for my own needs versus what future buyers might want?

acceptedAnswer.text: A home addition should solve your current needs first, but resale should still influence the design. Flexible rooms, good natural light, balanced proportions, and a layout that feels easy to live in tend to appeal to more buyers later. Highly specialized spaces can be useful, but they may limit the home’s marketability if they are too personalized. In neighborhoods like Pasadena, Glendale, and Los Angeles, the addition should also feel appropriate for the home’s architectural style and the surrounding area. That helps protect value by avoiding an overbuilt or awkward-looking result. The best strategy is usually to design a space that serves your family well now while staying broad enough to fit future use by someone else. That balance is what keeps an addition from becoming a liability when it is time to sell.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, the design should balance personal needs with broad market appeal. Rooms that are flexible, well-proportioned, and compatible with the home’s style usually hold value better than highly customized layouts. Avoid design choices that solve one problem but make the home harder to sell later.
